items.title: Spurs, Celtics, Grizzlies Lead NBA In Net Rating; Warriors Slide Without Stephen Curry
items.summary: Three teams have separated themselves in the NBA's efficiency rankings as the San Antonio Spurs (+11.4), Boston Celtics (+10.9) and Memphis Grizzlies (+10.3) are the only teams outscoring opponents by more than 10 points per 100 possessions. The Minnesota Timberwolves are just short at +9.7, built mostly on the league's best defense, which has sustained without Anthony Edwards. The Houston Rockets (+9.0) are next, driven largely by their offense. The Detroit Pistons (+6.5), Los Angeles Lakers (+6.4), New York Knicks (+6.3) and Portland Trail Blazers (+6.3) form the next tier. The Oklahoma City Thunder sit at +4.5 despite their injuries to Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren. The Golden State Warriors had the biggest drop this week, falling from +4.3 to -1.0. Stephen Curry has been sidelined with an oblique tear, and Golden State lost to the Spurs by 38 points and the New Orleans Pelicans by 21 without him. The Utah Jazz made the biggest gain, improving from -10.9 to -7.2. The Sacramento Kings (-14.0) and Milwaukee Bucks (-13.0) have the league's worst net ratings. The Charlotte Hornets are third-worst at -10.7, largely because of the league's lowest-rated offense that has struggled since the LaMelo Ball trade and injuries to Kon Knueppel and Brandon Miller.

items.title: Tom Thibodeau Open To NBA Return But Won't Pursue Jobs Before They Open
items.summary: Tom Thibodeau's name has come up as a possible replacement for coaches around the NBA, but a league source close to Thibodeau told The Athletic he will not communicate with any team, directly or indirectly, about interest in a job that has not opened. That approach could complicate matters for teams weighing a coaching change. Decision-makers will not be able to learn whether Thibodeau would want the job before deciding the fate of their current coach. Thibodeau is known to be interested in returning as a head coach when the right opportunity arises. There are currently no head coaching vacancies in the NBA. Thibodeau has been out of coaching since the New York Knicks fired him in early June 2025. He was dismissed shortly after leading New York to its first Eastern Conference finals appearance in 25 years. Doug Christie is in the last guaranteed season of his contract with the Sacramento Kings, which has raised speculation that a coaching change could be possible.
